title: Keep calibration values visible
summary: Diagnose a histogram range that silently sends a boundary measurement to overflow.
description: Repair TH1D* build_calibration_histogram(const std::vector<double>& values). Calibration measurements span 0 through 100 inclusive and must stay in visible 10-unit bins rather than disappearing into underflow or overflow.
requirements: Make the intended 0 through 100 calibration range visible, including the value 100.
Fill every input value exactly once.

examples.explanation: In ROOT the upper histogram edge belongs to overflow, so a [0,100) visible range does not contain x = 100.

hints: Inspect bin 0 and bin GetNbinsX()+1: they are underflow and overflow.
If visible bins must remain 10 units wide, extend the upper edge rather than stretching the bins.
learning_goal: Use underflow and overflow as evidence that a histogram range does not represent the intended sample.

curriculum.competency: Diagnose a histogram whose chosen range hides observations in underflow or overflow.
curriculum.misconception: A value equal to the histogram upper edge is contained in the last visible bin.
curriculum.observable_success: The learner preserves 10-unit bins while making every intended calibration value visible and verifies zero underflow/overflow.
curriculum.acceptance: A deliberately bad range produces observable under/overflow; the learner identifies and corrects the representation problem.

es.title: Mantén visibles los valores de calibración
es.summary: Diagnostica un rango de histograma que envía silenciosamente una medición de borde al overflow.
es.description: Repara TH1D* build_calibration_histogram(const std::vector<double>& values). Las mediciones de calibración van de 0 a 100 inclusive y deben permanecer en bins visibles de 10 unidades, sin desaparecer en underflow u overflow.
requirements: Mantén bins visibles de 10 unidades de ancho.
Haz visible el rango de calibración previsto de 0 a 100, incluido el valor 100.
Llena cada valor de entrada exactamente una vez.

examples.explanation: En ROOT el borde superior del histograma pertenece al overflow, por lo que un rango visible [0,100) no contiene x = 100.

hints: Inspecciona el bin 0 y el bin GetNbinsX()+1: son underflow y overflow.
Si los bins visibles deben seguir midiendo 10 unidades, extiende el borde superior en vez de estirar los bins.
es.learning_goal: Usar underflow y overflow como evidencia de que el rango de un histograma no representa la muestra prevista.
